messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: REDWOOD-INCIDENT: Elevated decode tail latency observed for hosted-inference region us-west-2. p99 has spiked to ~1.7s (baseline ~250ms). Auto-alert triggered. Thread created for triage.

maya patel: seeing this in the dashboards as well — sudden jump at 22:10 UTC, streaming endpoints more affected than sync. p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1700ms. Noticed an increase in page faults on GPUs about the same time.

ram singh: confirming. Logs show repeated kernel OOM/kpage faults on decode workers. Might be related to the kernel/compilepath change rolled yesterday: kernel-rt-2026.03 + compiler flag -ffast-decoder on the TRT build.

sasha lee: pinging @kevin o'brien and @ops-lead. Any prod deploys around that window?

kevin o'brien: I pushed the TRT/FlashAttention upgrade (trt-8.2.1 -> trt-8.2.3) and enabled the compiler flag batch at 21:35 UTC — rollout rate 30% then ramped to 100% by 21:55. No infra changes aside from the driver bump.

maya patel: timeline aligns. Telemetry: KV cache miss rate up ~18%, memory reclaim activity up on nodes running decode runtime. Streaming stalls correlate with KV eviction.

ram singh: grabbing debug from one affected instance. Attaching tail of dmesg: 
```
[22:11:03] NVRM: GPU page fault at 0x7f8a23... (0x000)
[22:11:03] kernel: nvmap: attempted reclaim -> swp->page_fault
[22:11:04] decode-runtime[pid=312]: WARNING: streaming stall detected, duration=420ms
```

infra-bot: Resource snapshot: node-gpu-45: mem.used=86%, swap.used=12%, oom_recoveries=3 in last 10m.

sasha lee: hypothesis: new compile flags / TRT micro-upgrade causing a working set increase (or different allocation pattern) that moves more state to pageable memory -> page faults -> tail stalls. Could also be a driver regression in 8.2.3.

maya patel: customer impact: two mid-sized customers on dedicated had elevated p99 errors; several hosted customers reported streaming timeouts ~22:12-22:20 UTC. Ops ticket #INC-4821 created.

ops-lead: Escalate? We should consider immediate mitigation: rollback compiler flag or roll back TRT driver. Which is faster?

ram singh: fastest is to rollout a targeted flag rollback (disable -ffast-decoder) on decode build via config flip per deployment group. Driver rollback requires kernel module coordination and node drains -> slower.

kevin o'brien: I can push a config flip to disable the flag for streaming pools in us-west-2. Command I will run: 
```bash
# flip feature flag for decode service
curl -XPOST https://infra-api.internal/v1/featureflip -d '{"service":"decode-runtime","flag":"fast_decode_enable","value":false,"scope":"us-west-2:streaming-pool"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

maya patel: while that's running, scale up fallback pool (quantized variant) and enable routing fallback for in-flight requests to lower-memory model variant. 

infra-bot: trigger accepted. Scaling streaming-fallback-pool +2 pods (GPU). ETA 4m.

kevin o'brien: flip initiated. Rolling disable to 100% in 3 waves to avoid new regressions. Watching metrics.

[22:19 UTC] maya patel: immediate p99 dropped from 1.7s -> 650ms after first wave, p95 back to ~300ms. Errors reduced.

sasha lee: logs from decode-host-12 show significantly fewer page faults after flip. dmesg snippet: 
```
[22:20:10] kernel: nvmap: reclaim: successful
[22:20:11] decode-runtime: INFO: stall resolved
```

ops-lead: good containment. Next steps: keep flag disabled for the rest of the region, create rollback PR for TRT driver upgrade to hold off until we have longer-term reproducer. Also run a controlled A/B test against a small pool with the flag enabled and extra tracing.

ram singh: filing follow-up issue: INVEST-420 - reproduce high page fault pattern with new compileflags + trt-8.2.3 on a lab cluster. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

kevin o'brien: I'll also check build artifacts; maybe the compiler optimization changed memory layout. Q: do we have perf traces (nvprof, CUPTI) from the timeframe?

maya patel: not yet. Requesting traces from affected nodes via runbook: <https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/paging-triage>. Collect stack traces and GPU alloc traces.

infra-bot: trace collection job STARTED on node-gpu-45. JobID=trace-1743219999-1. ETA 6m.

[22:32 UTC] maya patel: ops update to customers: small number saw degraded tail latency for ~10m between 22:10-22:20 UTC. We applied mitigation (disabled fast_decode flag, scaled fallback pool). No data exfiltration or errors beyond timeouts. Customer success notified.

sasha lee: handover to night oncall in 40m. Leaving runbook and mitigations in place. Will keep the flag disabled until repro.

ops-lead: assigning night oncall: @ram singh to take handoff. Please monitor p95/p99 for 2 hours and be ready to roll back more if needed.

ram singh: acknowledged. Handoff notes: mitigation = disabled fast_decode flag (us-west-2 streaming pools), scaled fallback pool +2, blocking TRT driver upgrade PR until INVEST-420 results. Monitoring alerts set: p99>700ms -> page oncall.

maya patel: adding checklist for postmortem: timeline, root cause hypotheses (compiler flag vs trt driver), reproducer steps, tenant impact, mitigation timeline, customer comms.

oncall-bot: NOTE: Reminder - link to live incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/1743219999.

ram singh: last check before handoff: p99 = 420ms, p95 = 310ms, error rate back to baseline. Leaving watchers. :white_check_mark:

kevin o'brien: I'll revert the TRT driver PR in staging and run the workload overnight. Will post findings in INVEST-420.

sasha lee: thanks everyone. If p99 rises again, escalate to infra-leads and consider rolling nodes to older driver.

infra-bot: SCAN COMPLETE: trace-1743219999-1 collected. Artifacts uploaded to https://artifacts.redwood/trace-1743219999-1.

ops-lead: handoff complete. Night oncall: ram singh.

ram singh: taking channel. Monitoring window started 22:45 UTC.

end of thread.
